links.comparator_used: Initial merged prompt (V1) used without refinement, compared with the optimized prompt (V3) after 3 iterations of clinician- and patient-informed refinement
links.outcome: Physician acceptance of draft suitability and patient preference for tone and overall quality
links.effect: Physician acceptance of draft suitability rose from 62% to 84% (P<.001) in the validation set (N=200). Patients preferred the optimized prompt for tone (62%) and quality (62%) versus <15% for the first prompt (P<.001). Positive sentiment in patient comments was 68% versus 23%. Hallucinations appeared in 6% (7/116) of original training-set messages and in none of the validation-set messages.
links.quote: When comparing responses created from the final prompt to the initial prompt, patient preference shifted to the optimized prompt (V3) based LLM-generated responses for tone ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%) and quality ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%), significantly higher than preference to the first iteration of prompt based LLM-generated response (<15% for both tone or overall quality) with P -value less than .001.

links.comparator_used: No direct comparator; clinicians' perceived effect of LLM drafts on InBasket workload, and patient blinded comparison of drafts against real human-written responses
links.outcome: Clinician perceived usefulness, cognitive load and InBasket time after production deployment of LLM draft replies
links.effect: 94% of surveyed clinicians would keep using and recommend the tool. 72% believed it can reduce cognitive load and 41% believed it can reduce InBasket time. 74% of drafts were rated helpful (761 rated messages). Survey response rate was 58% (40 clinicians).
links.tradeoff: Only 41% believed InBasket time would fall. The initial-prompt drafts were less preferred than human replies, and 6% of training-set drafts contained hallucinated information. Cognitive load was not measured with a validated questionnaire.
links.quote: Vast majority (94%) clinicians would like to keep using the ART technology and would recommend it to a colleague, 72% believe that LLM draft response can reduce cognitive load in dealing with InBasket messages, and 41% believe it has potential to reduce InBasket time.

design_hint: iterative prompt engineering with clinician and patient feedback
